turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Fireworks tonight on the river. Every year I take a hundred photos and they're all rubbish.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fireworks really need the camera to stay still for a second or two. Do you have a tripod, or anything to rest the camera on?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could bring the little one from the drawer.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Great. Set focus manually to infinity, use a low ISO, and an exposure of about two to four seconds. That turns sparks into long trails.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My camera does have a manual mode, I've just never touched it.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Have a go in your living room before you leave, just to find the settings. It's much easier than fumbling in the dark.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Go a bit wider than you think, because you can't predict where they'll burst. If you get the river in the bottom, the reflections double the show.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Right. This might finally be the year.
